Hi team,

Attached is the updated pipeline workbook (tab "ACME - reserve ask"). Acme just moved to verbal commitment for a Q1 pilot + subsequent production reserve if pilot KPIs hit. High-level: pilot needs ~64 A100-equivalent slots for 4 weeks (burstable); production asks for a 12-month committed pool of 120 A100-eq starting Feb 1 with a soft ramp in January.

Asks:
- Can Infra confirm whether we can allocate a 120-slot reserved pool starting 2029-02-01 under the Dedicated product?
- Finance: what's the minimum commit term we should propose to match the unit economics? (Jordan included a starter term sheet draft)

I'm leaving today at 3pm PT but wanted to get this into the weekly handoff so we can lock capacity early.

Thanks,
Jordan

Subject: Re: Weekly fleet handoff: reserve plan for upcoming deals & runway adjustments

Jordan / team,

Quick read of the ask: 120 A100-eq sounds doable on paper but we need to reconcile with current committed pools (2 enterprise commits and scheduled maintenance in Jan). Two points:

1) Lead time: to guarantee 120 reserved slots we need a signed PO or SOW by 2028-12-15 to pull capacity in Feb without risking overcommit. Otherwise we should propose a staged reserve (40 -> 80 -> 120) tied to milestone payments.

2) Ops constraints: January maintenance window (2029-01-10 to 2029-01-14) removes ~8% of available capacity in our primary region; recommend we either shift start to Feb 15 or factor in burst credits.

Can Infra comment on whether burst credits (short-term) are available for the pilot (64 slots for 4 weeks)? If yes, we can avoid a hard commit for pilot.

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Weekly fleet handoff: reserve plan for upcoming deals & runway adjustments

Thanks for the quick analysis. A few clarifications from Sales perspective:

- Acme wants a firm start date in contract language (they prefer early Feb). They are comfortable with staged billing but want "logical capacity continuity" for the pilot to production transition.
- The pilot is expected to generate 750M tokens/day during peak periods (this affects both batching config and inferred KV cache sizing).

Action items I suggest this week:
1) Infra (Karthik/Marcus) — confirm feasibility of burst credits for pilot and whether a staged reserve plan is supported by the reservation UI/API. If staged is supported we can push a 40/80/120 ramp tied to milestone invoices.
2) Finance (Laura/Ben) — please confirm the minimum monetary commit that keeps us within our margin targets for the dedicated pool. Also confirm whether we can accept a three-month trial at a lower per-token price as a bridge.
3) Sales (Jordan/Soojin) — I'll draft a short paragraph for the SOW covering ramp and fallback to Hosted tiers if capacity pressure hits 95% utilization for 48+ hours.

I'll loop in Acme procurement once we have an infra feasibility answer.

-Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-11-06T14:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Weekly fleet handoff: reserve plan for upcoming deals & runway adjustments

Short answer: pilot burst for 64 A100-eq for 4 weeks = feasible with burst credits, but with caveats. Details:

- Available pool: we can carve out pilot capacity using existing burst pool for up to 6 weeks without changing long-term capacity allocations. That will consume ~12% of the current burst budget for the quarter.
- Staged reserve: our reservation API supports incremental slot increases (we can push from 40 -> 80 -> 120 programmatically) but the billing contract must capture the committed floor at each milestone.
- Ops note: if the pilot runs into consistent 85%+ utilization, we will need to either (a) auto-fall back to Hosted for overflow, or (b) move additional capacity from non-critical reserved pools (requires approvals).

I'll prepare a short ops runbook that maps utilization thresholds to automated fallback actions and notify on-call.

Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure Engineering
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-11-07T10:09:00-08:00
Subject: Redwood Dedicated: proposal for pilot / production ramp (SOW summary)

Sarah / ACME team,

Thanks again for the productive call. Per our internal availability check, here's the proposal summary we discussed:

- Pilot: 64 A100-equivalent slots, 4-week duration, start target week of 2029-01-22 (backup start 2029-02-05); covered by burst credits to avoid a hard commit during pilot.
- Production reserved pool: target 120 A100-eq beginning 2029-02-15 with a staged billing ramp (40 / 80 / 120 tied to milestone payments).
- SLA: 99.9%% uptime for reserved pool; automatic overflow to Hosted for transient >95%% utilization for >48 hours.
- Terms: 12-month minimum for production reserved pool; Finance open to a 3-month bridge pricing for pilot-to-prod transition.

Attached: short SOW paragraph and the internal forecast workbook. Please review the dates and milestone language; Jordan and I can update and reissue a clean SOW if these look good.

Next step: Sarah, can procurement confirm whether ACME can sign an SOW with staged billing and milestone acceptance? If yes, we'll target a PO by 2028-12-12 to secure capacity.

Best,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-11-08T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated: proposal for pilot / production ramp (SOW summary)

Hi Soojin / Jordan,

Thanks for the SOW summary — procurement is OK in principle with staged billing tied to milestones, but we need two clarifications before routing a PO to legal:

1) Can you confirm the fallback mechanics to Hosted (explicitly: latency SLA and cost deltas when overflow happens)?
2) Please clarify whether burst credits for the pilot will be invoiced or treated as a platform credit; ACME prefers not to be billed for pilot burst unless explicitly accepted.

If you can get us a short one-page addendum that answers (1) + (2), procurement will start the PO process this week.

Sarah Liu
Head of Procurement
Acme Analytics
